blocks.prompt: 6 Show that \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\) has a relative minimum at \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof with the Second Derivative Test; the variable is in the base and in the power.
Given \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\), defined for \(x > 0\).
Plan: logarithmic differentiation for \(f'\), show \(f'\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 0\), then \(f''\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) > 0\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\), \(x > 0\).
To show: relative minimum at \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\).
Method: neither the power rule nor the exponential rule fits \(x^{x^{2}}\), so take logarithms first (2.6); then the Second Derivative Test.

Take logarithms
Let \(y = x^{x^{2}}\).
\[\ln y = x^{2}\ln x\]
Why: \(\ln a^{b} = b\ln a\) brings the power down.

Differentiate
\[\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\ln x + x^{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[f'(x) = x^{x^{2}}\,x\,(1 + 2\ln x)\]
\[= x^{x^{2} + 1}(1 + 2\ln x)\]
Why: implicit differentiation on the left, product rule on the right; then multiply by \(y = x^{x^{2}}\).

Stationary point
\[1 + 2\ln x = 0 \Rightarrow \ln x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[x = e^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\]
Why: \(x^{x^{2} + 1} > 0\) for \(x > 0\), so only the bracket can be zero.

Second derivative at the point
Write \(f'(x) = g(x)h(x)\), \(g = x^{x^{2} + 1}\), \(h = 1 + 2\ln x\):
\[f''(x) = g'(x)h(x) + g(x)h'(x)\]
At \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\), \(h = 0\) and \(h' = \frac{2}{x}\):
\[f''\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = x^{x^{2} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{2}{x} = 2x^{x^{2}}\]
Why: product rule; the first term vanishes because \(h = 0\), so we never need \(g'\).

Its sign
\[x^{2} = \dfrac{1}{e},\quad x^{x^{2}} = \left(e^{-1/2}\right)^{1/e} = e^{-\frac{1}{2e}}\]
\[f''\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 2e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} > 0\]
Why: a power of \(e\) is always positive. By the Second Derivative Test \(f\) has a relative minimum here.

Minimum value
\[f\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} \approx 0.832\]
Why: it is the same expression \(x^{x^{2}}\) found above.
Check: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}} \approx 0.607\); \(f(0.5) = 0.5^{0.25} \approx 0.841\) and \(f(0.7) = 0.7^{0.49} \approx 0.839\) are both larger than 0.832.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(f'\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 0\) and \(f''\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 2e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} > 0\), so \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\) has a relative minimum at \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\) (minimum value \(e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} \approx 0.832\)).
